- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon, especially after sharp price spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 2–5%.
- Underestimate in the final 5–10 days of the forecast; adjust upward by 1–3% to align with recent mean reversion trends.
- If the 30-day history shows a clear upward trend, model tends to overreact; dampen forecast slope by 10–15%.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >10% in the first 5 days, reduce subsequent forecast values by 5–10% to avoid momentum overcorrection.
- When true outcome is consistently 5–10% below forecast, shift forecast mean downward by 3–5% to reflect underestimation bias.
- Avoid forecasting “peak” values too early; delay peak prediction by 2–3 days if recent history shows delayed peak behavior.
- If forecast is consistently 5–10% above true outcome across all days, reduce forecast by 5–8% globally to correct for systematic overconfidence.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below forecast), adjust forecast to follow the mean of the last 7–10 days.
